newsitem.title: EGYPT: Suez Canal revenues decline in first nine months.
newsitem.headline: Suez Canal revenues decline in first nine months.

text.p: Suez Canal revenues continued a downtrend to $1.358 billion in the first nine months of 1996 from $1.453 billion in the same period last year, the Suez Canal Authority (SCA) statistics department said on Tuesday.
Revenue from the canal in September amounted to $120 million against $150 million in the same month of 1995, it added.
The department said that 11,019 ships used the canal in the first nine months of 1996. It did not give comparative figures.
Revenues from the Suez Canal form one of the four major foreign currency earners in Egypt.
Officials from the Egyptian parliament's transportation committee and the SCA met on Monday to discuss the reasons behind the decline in revenues
SCA Chairman Ahmed Fadel said the authority was working to make canal transit time and fees more competitive and there were continuous contacts to persuade oil exporters to use the canal.
